label: sparse early-input conjunction (first token r, input r/j/u after u/q/j/e/v)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.05% of steps, about 0.6% of sequences). It fires mostly during the original phase at t=3-4 (83% of mass is in the original phase; it never fires at t=0-1). It also fires weakly on <DEL> and on early copy steps. Each token factor enriches it on its own: input r/j/u (up to 8x), previous input u/q/j/e/v (up to 12x), first token r (13x). But no conjunction of these reaches F1 above 0.15. The strongest examples are sequences starting with r (for example r a c j [r]), where the input is r or j at t=3-4 right after u/q/j. The recorded predicate is precise (about 0.3) but covers only about 10% of the mass. The feature looks like a hashed direction in the hidden state, driven by specific combinations of early tokens, rather than one interpretable property. It does not fire at t<2, rarely fires late in the copy phase, and never fires when copying has gone wrong. No magnitude claims beyond the fact that the top activations come from sequences starting with r.
